kind: PRODUCTION glue, authored as a phase-13 gate fix round. Task 13.1's Step 2 ('red -> glue fixes -> green — this is the harness proving itself') names the plugin COMPOSITION ROOT as 13.1's production work, and 13.1 landed without it: a recorded deviation in STATE.json tasks['13.1'].deviations ('the plugin tool-map binding not done'). At HEAD conductor/plugin/index.ts builds its `tool` map from CONDUCTOR_TOOL_NAMES with `execute: handlerNotBound(name)` for all 22 names, so NOT ONE committed handleX handler is reachable through the plugin opencode actually loads. This task binds them, and — because the same binding is what first populates the §3.5 session registry with SUB-SESSION entries — it is also the only context in which the phase-13 gate's MAJOR 6 (the three literal gate-snapshot fields at the tool.execute.before seam) can be closed with a behavioural test rather than a source guard. Delivered as TWO commits: CR-1 binds the tools, CR-2 derives the snapshot.

specGaps: CR-SG-1 (no run is live when a tool is called). Most handlers need a runId, and store.currentRun() can legitimately return null (a fresh repo, an archived run). RESOLUTION: the binding refuses with a legible, actionable message naming the tool and what to do instead — it never fabricates a run id, never creates a run as a side effect of a stage tool, and never lets a null propagate into a handler as an empty string. conductor_setup, conductor_status and conductor_forget_stale are the three that must still work with no run.

CR-SG-2 (arg mapping is where a silent lie would live). Every tool's declared `args` shape in plugin/index.ts specs already exists; the binding must pass each through to its handler's own field, and MUST NOT invent a default for a field the model was supposed to supply. C-047 is the recorded precedent: declaring conductor_decide's options as a bare string array made the tool UNABLE TO SUCCEED, because a string carries no score and the composition root may not fabricate one. A missing required arg is a refusal, not a default.

CR-SG-3 (the TreeState the wave driver needs). handleDispatchWave requires a WaveTreeState whose isFrozen reads the REAL per-tree verify marker, and whose onClear fires when a marker is removed. A stub returning `false` would make the §3.5 freeze admission dead on the driver side exactly as `verifyInFlightTree: null` does on the gate side — the same defect twice. RESOLUTION: one marker-backed implementation, built from the same exported marker enumeration CR-2 uses for the gate, so a freeze is one fact read by both seams and not two implementations that can disagree.

CR-SG-4 (packs). Handlers take `packs: Record<string,string>` for the doctrine the sub-session prompts carry. The factory never calls loadPacks at HEAD. RESOLUTION: load once, lazily, alongside the workspace; a missing pack is LOUD on the §7.1 sink and leaves the tools refusing — §6.4 fail-closed — rather than dispatching sub-sessions with no doctrine, which is the silent-degradation shape §3.8 exists to forbid.

CR-SG-5 (this task does not touch the e2e). conductor/tests/e2e.test.ts drives handlers directly today; rewriting its five scenarios to drive through the bound tool map is the phase-13 e2e fix round's job and is deliberately NOT taken here. What this task owes is that the rewrite becomes POSSIBLE. Any e2e change beyond keeping it green is out of scope.
knownPartialCoverage: 13.1-cr-packs-loaded-fail-closed is bound in its POSITIVE half only, and this is recorded rather than quietly counted as covered. The bound half is strong: the test drives a guaranteed-red full verify so adapter/tools.ts's bounded DEBUG loop is reached, and asserts the sub-session prompt STARTS WITH the byte-for-byte contents of conductor/doctrine/debug.md read from disk by the test — a binding that hands `packs: {}` produces no dispatch at all (tools.ts:4132-4139 refuses before dispatching when the pack set has no debug.md) and a binding that hands a paraphrase fails the verbatim comparison. The UNBOUND half is 'a MISSING pack is reported at error level on the §7.1 sink and the tools refuse': the packs ship with the harness, loadPacks takes a doctrineDir the composition root resolves from its own module URL, and no config or env override exists anywhere in conductor/, so manufacturing the condition means renaming a tracked repo file or standing up a copied tree with working module resolution. DEFERRED TO CR-2, test first: if the doctrine directory is made injectable there, the half becomes a three-line test. The row text is deliberately NOT weakened to match the coverage — editing an acceptance row to fit the test that was written is the C-076 failure (rewrite the claim instead of the thing), and it is the reason M7 exists.

the C-047 TWIN, found by binding the tools and reachable only because they are now bound: plugin/index.ts declares conductor_queue_amend's `ops` as `S.array(S.string())` while core/queue-amend.ts:21-24 QueueAmendOp is `{op:'add'|'update', item: QueueItem} | {op:'remove', id: string}`, so a model that follows the declared schema hands strings, core's amend parse refuses them, and the tool CANNOT SUCCEED — the identical defect C-047 recorded for conductor_decide's scored options. The DECLARATION is not what is wrong — core/queue-amend.ts:82 parseAmendOps(raw: readonly string[]) is the committed bridge that turns exactly that declared wire shape into the closed union, and tools-9.4b.test.ts:2940 unit-pins it in a test whose own title calls it 'the binding Task 9.6 needs'. The defect is that NOTHING calls it: the composition root casts the declared strings straight into the handler's field. The fix is to call parseAmendOps on the way in and to refuse with its own `why` when a parse fails — not to redeclare the argument, and never to fabricate the missing structure. Asserted by driving a real amendment through the bound tool with ops built to the DECLARED shape and requiring it to be APPLIED, and by a malformed op being refused with the parser's message naming the offending position; and conductor/tests/tool-binding.test.ts's [C-047-shape] guard, green over this defect today, is sharpened until it is not

the `queueEntry` zod declaration this task added to plugin/index.ts (so conductor_queue_amend's ops can declare the structure the handler requires) is a SECOND spelling of core's §2.4 QueueItem, and this build's most-repeated defect class is two spellings of one fact. Core's validateQueue remains the only validator — a drift is a legible refusal, not corruption — but it must not drift unobserved: the declared field set is checked against core's own QueueItem/SCHEMAS.Queue field set derived at run time, with any field core carries that a tool argument legitimately should not declare listed in a NAMED, justified exclusion in the test, so a new core field forces a decision rather than silently vanishing

conductor_status must work before any run exists, and the shape it returns then is NOT allowed to be a hand-built literal the type system never sees: adapter/tools.ts:808-814 StatusResult declares `runId: string` and `state: RunState`, both non-nullable, so the no-run branch is a SECOND shape returned through an `unknown`-typed binding where no compiler checks it and a field added to StatusResult drifts silently. Bind it to the handler's own result: the runless return carries EXACTLY the key set handleStatus produces for a real run (derived at run time from a live call, never from a list copied into the test), with the absent run reported as null rather than invented — so growing StatusResult without growing the runless shape is red

adapter/evidence.ts liveVerifyTrees applies the SAME liveness rule the verify path applies, because a second definition of 'live' is the very defect the single-source row exists to prevent: runVerify:790-807 honours a marker only when `pidAlive(marker.pid) && now() - marker.startMs <= staleMarkerMs`, and breaks a dead-pid or over-age marker with the comment 'a crashed run can never wedge a tree'. An enumeration that reports every marker FILE present reintroduces exactly that wedge one seam over — a crashed verify would hold every write-capable wave member for its tree forever and, once CR-2 lands, deny every edit to that tree forever. Asserted both ways: a marker whose pid is alive and fresh IS reported, and a marker with a dead pid, and one whose startMs is older than staleMarkerMs, are BOTH absent from the result — while remaining on disk, because a read-only enumeration must not delete another party's marker (that is runVerify's move, under §4.3)

conductor_setup refuses the way all 21 other tools refuse — by THROWING, which is what opencode reads back to the model — and NOT by returning a refusal as ordinary data: a configured repo without `reconfigure:true` throws adapter/tools.ts:8852-8858's message, while the first-run leg is asserted where a first run actually happens, in a repo with NO .conductor/config.json. The composition root may not soften a handler's refusal channel to satisfy a fixture that configured the repo before calling the first-run tool

the plugin's rebindable journal forwards `flushSync` to the run-bound journal: adapter/tools.ts:2427-2434 and :5014-5026 forward it only when the sink they were handed carries one, so without the forward a verify's evidence records sit unflushed while the tool that wrote them returns — asserted by reading the run's journal.jsonl off disk immediately after a bound tool returns and finding the records the tool wrote already durable

the §3.6 one-shot grant is END-TO-END: handleOverride mints into the plugin's overrideGrants map and the SAME map reaches gateBeforeToolCall, so the next matching edit is converted from deny to allow and the grant is consumed — a grant with no consumer is a dead hatch, which is what the seam was before this round. Both halves asserted: the first edit after the override lands, the second identical edit is denied again

conductor_override refuses when the calling session carries no §3.5 registry itemId rather than choosing one: core/tool-bindings.ts lists itemId as infrastructure the composition root reads from the registry, and an orchestrator session with no item assignment has none — fabricating one would spend the wrong item's §2.1 override budget and write the taint onto the wrong item. The refusal names §3.6 and the run's state is byte-identical afterwards

CR-2: the gate's fileScope and testScope are DERIVED PER CALL from the calling session's registry entry — its itemId's persisted item.fileScope / item.testScope — rather than the HEAD literals `[]`: an implementer session registered to item I1 is ALLOWED an edit inside I1's fileScope and DENIED one outside it, and a test-writer session is allowed inside testScope and denied inside fileScope. CR-2: verifyInFlightTree is derived from the LIVE marker set and translated slug->path through the committed adapter/tools.ts:2376 verifyInFlightTreeFor, so §3.5's freeze fires exactly where core/gates-edit.ts:196-198 says: while a marker is live for tree T, an edit by a session whose tree is T is DENIED, an edit by a session in a DIFFERENT tree is ALLOWED, and once the marker clears the same denied edit succeeds.
